We are Artemis TECH, a team passionate about programming, technology, and innovation. Our mission is to transform ideas into digital solutions through software development, creativity, and collaborative work.

We specialize in exploring new technological possibilities, designing applications, and developing projects that address real-world needs. We believe that every challenge represents an opportunity to learn, improve, and push beyond our own limits.
summary: Terra Analog Explorer is an interactive geospatial web platform created to bridge Earth observation with Lunar and Martian surface exploration. Then adventure begins by projecting planetary landing targets and terrestrial terrains into a unified five-dimensional geophysical space—powered by official orbital archives from NASA PDS , NASA POWER, NASA Worldview GIBS, and ESA Copernicus Sentinel-1 SAR. From there, the platform evaluates two complementary groups of Earth sites: established NASA calibration benchmarks and underexplored high-potential terrains (such as Pampa de la Joya and Andahua in Peru). Using a hybrid Cosine and Euclidean similarity model, our system reveals a critical engineering insight: visual resemblance alone isn´t enough, it is necessary to quantify both subsystem alignment and physical analogy breakdowns—such as reduced gravity, ultra-high vacuum, and radiation—prevents costly hardware testing mismatches. We implemented an early interactive exploration mode, where users tune subsystem priority weights in real time across Lunar and Martian targets, audit exact satellite granule provenance, and export downloadable Mission Technical Briefs. Designed to reduce data friction for mission planners, planetary scientists, and aerospace engineers, Planetary Analog Finder turns vast orbital archives into traceable field-validation decisions. We turn planetary data into analog discovery, and analog discovery into mission readiness.
details:
Humanity has long dreamed of conquering our Moon and Mars. The plan is finally underway, and we must prepare rigorously for the harsh conditions that lurk throughout the universe. In anticipation of this, here at home—on planet Earth—hundreds of satellite images and a wealth of collected data have been stored away for years, ready to be put to use.

What if the Moon and Mars could tell us where on Earth to prepare for our next giant leap? Our app, Terra Analog Explore, solves the challenge by turning multi-dimensional orbital data into traceable engineering decisions, allowing mission planners to uncover hidden terrestrial proving grounds while pinpointing the exact physical limits where space simulation must take over.
